profile.name: Mudivarthi Vishwak Sai
profile.title: Aspiring VLSI Design Verification Engineer | RTL Design Engineer

projects.title: FIFO RTL Design and Verification
projects.description: Designed and verified a synchronous FIFO using Verilog, with control logic and testbench-driven simulation.
projects.detail: Developed a UVM-based verification environment for a 16-depth, 8-bit synchronous FIFO using SystemVerilog. Implemented reusable UVM components, including sequence, driver, monitor, agent, environment, and test. Created stimulus to verify FIFO read and write operations. Implemented a scoreboard with a reference model to check data integrity and FIFO ordering. Verified full and empty conditions, boundary cases, and simultaneous read/write operations. Simulated and debugged the testbench using QuestaSim and EDA Playground.

projects.title: UART Transmitter and Receiver
projects.description: Explored UART TX/RX behavior using SystemVerilog testbench development and waveform analysis.
projects.detail: Designed and verified a UART transmitter and receiver using SystemVerilog RTL. Developed a UVM-based testbench to automate functional verification. Implemented UVM components including sequences, driver, monitor, agent, and environment. Verified UART data transmission and reception under different test scenarios. Analyzed simulation waveforms using QuestaSim/EDA Playground to validate functionality. Strengthened understanding of RTL design, UVM methodology, and functional verification.

projects.title: Tri-State Buffer Design
projects.description: Implemented and simulated an enable-controlled tri-state buffer, including high-impedance output behavior.
projects.detail: Designed and implemented a Tri-State Buffer using Verilog HDL with enable-controlled data flow Implemented high-impedance (Hi-Z) functionality when the enable signal is disabled. Developed a SystemVerilog testbench to verify the buffer's functional behavior. Tested all input combinations to validate data propagation and Hi-Z output conditions. Performed RTL simulation and analyzed waveforms to verify the design functionality.

articles.title: Blocking vs Non-blocking Assignments
articles.summary: Understand procedural assignment timing and why sequential logic typically uses non-blocking assignments.
articles.code: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin\n  q <= d; // update after the time step\nend
articles.takeaway: Use blocking assignments for many combinational procedural calculations and non-blocking assignments for clocked state updates, following the coding style required by your project.

articles.title: Latch Inference and How to Avoid It
articles.summary: Learn why incomplete combinational assignments can infer storage unintentionally.
articles.takeaway: Assign every output on every path in combinational logic.

articles.title: FIFO Full and Empty Logic
articles.summary: Explore pointer relationships and status-flag reasoning in FIFO designs.
articles.code: // Example only: exact logic depends on FIFO architecture\nempty = (wr_ptr == rd_ptr);
articles.takeaway: Pointer wrap, extra pointer bits, and memory depth determine the correct full/empty equations.

articles.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Reset
articles.summary: Compare reset behavior relative to the active clock edge.
articles.takeaway: Choose reset strategy based on the design specification and reset-domain requirements.

articles.title: Moore vs Mealy State Machines
articles.summary: Compare outputs that depend on state alone with outputs that also depend on inputs.
articles.code: // Moore: output is a function of current state\nassign out = (state == ACTIVE);
articles.takeaway: Choose the FSM style based on timing, latency, and output-glitch requirements.

articles.title: Assertions and Functional Coverage
articles.summary: Use properties to catch temporal failures and coverage to measure exercised scenarios.
articles.takeaway: Assertions check behavior; coverage helps identify scenarios your tests have not exercised.
